title: Central model selection and fallback
summary: Owner goal of 3 November 2026: choose CLI, model and thinking level in one place, never stand still when a quota is spent or a provider rejects a model, and log every switch on the management page. The inventory of develop d63df0be4 finds quota admission shared by local runs, remote claims, review aspects, grade, chat and one-shots, but bypassed by the merge resolver, the local provider-limit skip and non-one-shot aspect paths. Deep review is never downgraded, review settings are per project step (the 72-PUT switch of 2 and 3 November), and capacity rejections never switch the model; the rate-limit-before-capacity classifier order explains the 60-minute Codex block of 2 November. Three alternatives compared; Option B recommended: a pure selection planner in the contracts package behind one ModelSelectionService, a 90-day selection ledger with API and a CLI Management view, a workspace policy per consumer class with project overrides, and eight ordered cards starting with one provider switch for every consumer.

# One provider switch for every consumer class

Source: `docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html` (AGT-3459). Read AGENTS.md, the Dossier sections Inventory, Recommendation and Open decisions, and `docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html` when touching run-outcome classification. Use each Dossier recommendation (D1 to D10) as the working decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another option, and record the option implemented. Frontend work uses central tokens and existing components and obeys the admin flat-surface contract (no coloured left accent bars, light and dark). Never edit workspace metadata or project folders directly; use the API. Git ownership stays with the platform. This is one bounded slice; scope outside its criteria stays in sibling cards.

## Goal
Make the manual 72-PUT review-step switch of 2 and 3 November 2026 unnecessary. One workspace action ("conserve provider X until its reset", today's `CliFallbackPreferenceService`, `PUT /api/cli/quota/fallback-preference`) must move every consumer class away from that provider.

## Deliver
1. Apply the active preference in every consumer that chooses a model today: remote review aspects including deep review (`V1ReviewPlaneEndpoints.cs` `ApplyQuotaFallbackToAspects`, remove the deep-review and immutable-plan exceptions for the operator switch only; quota-cap behaviour for deep review stays as is), the review grade (`CodeReviewGradeModelSelector`), local aspects, the merge-conflict resolver (`ProjectRunner.cs:2176-2217`), orchestrator chat, one-shots, and the card-creation recommendation (`TaskCrudEndpoints.cs:1051-1079`; do not rewrite existing pins).
2. Review consumers take only a target of the same Token Economy capability class; if none exists the result is wait with a reason, not a downgrade.
3. Add `GET /api/model-selection/effective?project=&pipelineType=` returning, per consumer class and step, the configured route, the effective route and the rule (`consumer-default`, `operator-switch`, `quota-cap`, `pin`).
4. Show the effective route next to the preference toggle in the CLI Management overlay (one line per consumer class).
5. The preference ends at its `ExpiresAt` as today; all consumers then return to their configured routes.

## Acceptance
- With 12 projects × 3 pipeline types configured on Claude review steps, one PUT of the preference makes `/effective` report Codex for all 36 review routes including deep review and grade (integration test).
- Expiry of the preference returns all 36 routes to Claude without any per-step write (test with a fake clock).
- Card creation without a model while the preference is active recommends the equivalent route; existing pinned cards are unchanged on disk.
- A review consumer with no same-class equivalent reports wait with rule and reason; unit tests cover the class filter.

## Tests
Add the unit, integration and Playwright tests named in the acceptance criteria; run the affected backend and frontend suites and report the results.

# Selection ledger and API

Source: `docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html` (AGT-3459). Read AGENTS.md, the Dossier sections Inventory, Recommendation and Open decisions, and `docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html` when touching run-outcome classification. Never edit workspace metadata or project folders directly; use the API. Git ownership stays with the platform. This is one bounded slice; scope outside its criteria stays in sibling cards.

## Goal
Record every non-trivial model selection in one workspace log the owner can read.

## Deliver
1. `ModelSelectionLedger` writing daily JSONL under `<TaskRepository>/.runtime/model-selection/<yyyy-MM-dd>.jsonl` with the schema in the Dossier (id, at, kind, consumer, host, project, pipelineType, stepId, taskKey, attemptId, round, from, to, rule, reason, evidence excerpt redacted to 300 characters, quota snapshot, equivalence, returnToPrimaryAt, closesId, pricePerMTok). One writer; atomic appends.
2. Retention: delete files older than 90 days; keep a daily summary (counts per provider, rule, consumer) for 400 days.
3. In-memory projection of active fallbacks and health marks, rebuilt from the last 14 days at start.
4. Routes: `GET /api/model-selection/events` (filters provider, project, consumer, rule, from, to, cursor; newest first), `GET /api/model-selection/active`, `POST /api/model-selection/events` (runner scope, idempotent by id). Declare route permissions in the IAM route inventory.
5. Writers: `QuotaAdmissionRecorder` (all emit methods), one-shot dispatch, review-plane fallback, `ProviderRejectionContinuation`, the remote claim path; Task Server and runner post through the ingestion route with bounded retry. Collapse repeated identical waiting events per card into one entry with a count.
6. Timeline events `QuotaAdmissionDecision` and `QuotaFallbackActivated` gain a `selectionEventId` detail.

## Acceptance
- Unit tests: schema round-trip, redaction, retention deletion at day 91, summary kept, collapse of repeated waits.
- Integration test: a quota fallback on a remote claim, a one-shot fallback and a provider-rejection continuation each produce exactly one ledger entry visible through the events route with the right filters.
- Ingestion rejects non-runner principals (route permission test) and is idempotent on a repeated id.
- Active projection after restart equals the projection before restart (test).

## Tests
Add the unit, integration and Playwright tests named in the acceptance criteria; run the affected backend and frontend suites and report the results.

# Capacity and model rejections switch the model

Source: `docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html` (AGT-3459). Read AGENTS.md, the Dossier sections Inventory, Recommendation and Open decisions, and `docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html` when touching run-outcome classification. Use each Dossier recommendation (D1 to D10) as the working decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another option, and record the option implemented. Frontend work uses central tokens and existing components and obeys the admin flat-surface contract (no coloured left accent bars, light and dark). Never edit workspace metadata or project folders directly; use the API. Git ownership stays with the platform. This is one bounded slice; scope outside its criteria stays in sibling cards.

## Goal
A provider rejection of one model must not stop work and must not block the whole provider. Incident: 2 November 2026 15:37 UTC, Codex "Selected model is at capacity" blocked every Codex claim for 60 minutes.

## Deliver
1. Reproduce: build a fixture from the 2 November run output (ask the operator for the redacted log through the card if it is not in the job folder) and show the current classification path. If the log cannot be obtained, use a synthetic fixture containing the capacity line plus a retry line with a rate-limit phrase and state that in the result.
2. In `ProviderAccessClassifier`, check capacity signals before rate-limit signals when both are present without an explicit reset; add tests for each ordering.
3. Model health marks per model and host: capacity (15 minutes or the provider retry hint), model-unavailable (until the next catalogue refresh), unauthorized (provider on that host until a successful probe). A capacity mark never sets the provider-wide `UnknownLimitTtl` limit.
4. After the bounded same-session capacity retries, the next fresh attempt selects the same-provider sibling (`ModelRoutingPolicyRegistry.ProviderRejectionFallback`) or else the cross-provider equivalent (`ModelEquivalenceCatalog`), subject to floor and host acceptance; in the monolith claim path, the Task Server recovery and the local runner (which today ignores `PendingIntent.ModelFallback`).
5. Write health-marked, switched and health-cleared events to the ledger when MS-2 is present; otherwise to the existing timeline.

## Acceptance
- Fixture test: the 2 November output (or the documented synthetic fixture) classifies as ModelCapacity and leads to no provider-wide limit.
- Runner test: capacity on gpt-6-sol marks only that model on that host; a claim for a gpt-5.6-sol card on the same host proceeds.
- Monolith, Task Server and local runner tests: after retries are exhausted the next attempt uses the sibling, and with the sibling also marked, the cross-provider equivalent.
- Unauthorized on one host switches provider for claims on that host only (test).

## Tests
Add the unit, integration and Playwright tests named in the acceptance criteria; run the affected backend and frontend suites and report the results.

## Deliver

implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Hysteresis, cost guard and return to primary

Source: `docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html` (AGT-3459). Read AGENTS.md, the Dossier sections Inventory, Recommendation and Open decisions, and `docs/concepts/orchestrator-drive-to-conclusion.html` when touching run-outcome classification. Use each Dossier recommendation (D1 to D10) as the working decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another option, and record the option implemented. Frontend work uses central tokens and existing components and obeys the admin flat-surface contract (no coloured left accent bars, light and dark). Never edit workspace metadata or project folders directly; use the API. Git ownership stays with the platform. This is one bounded slice; scope outside its criteria stays in sibling cards.

## Goal
No flapping near the cap, no silent cost increase, and a recorded return to the primary.

## Deliver
1. Return rule: a capped provider becomes primary again only after the window reset, or after usage is at least `returnBelowCapPoints` (default 10) below the cap for `minDwellMinutes` (default 30). Suspicious snapshots count as blocked.
2. The projected cap check also applies to the fallback target; if the target would cross its cap, the result is wait.
3. Cost guard: a fallback whose price per MTok exceeds the primary by more than `costGuardFactor` (default 2.0, per consumer class) needs an explicit policy entry or the operator switch; otherwise wait with rule `cost-guard`.
4. `returned` ledger events close the matching switch (`closesId`); the active strip empties accordingly.

## Acceptance
- Simulation test over recorded quota history (`QuotaHistoryStore` fixtures) oscillating between 94 and 96 %: at most one switch and one return per window.
- Cost guard tests for factor below, at and above the limit, and with an explicit policy entry.
- Fallback target near its own cap yields wait (test).
- Return events close switches and the active projection updates (test).

## Tests
Add the unit, integration and Playwright tests named in the acceptance criteria; run the affected backend and frontend suites and report the results.
